title: 3D in vitro culture system to study collective migration in mammary organoid epithelium
protocol: Put two 10 cm Petri dishes and surgery tools on the surgery table.
Turn on the dry glass bead sterilizer.
Turn on the 37°C heat block and 37°C shaker in the tissue culture room.
Warm up a DMEM/F12 bottle to room temperature in the tissue culture hood.
Add 0.02 g of collagenase to a 15 mL tube containing warm 9.3 mL of DMEM/F12.
Place the tube on a 37°C shaker.
Add 0.5 mL of FBS, 200 μL of 100 mg/mL trypsin, 10 μL of 50 mg/mL gentamicin, and 25 μL of 2 mg/mL insulin to the collagenase solution.
Sterilize the solution by running it through a 0.22 μm vacuum filter.
Add collagenase to the medium early to allow more time for it to dissolve.
Disinfect dissecting tools by heat in a glass bead sterilizer at 280°C for 1 min.
Cool surgical tools on an open Petri dish.
Sterilize all surgical supplies, a surgical board covered in aluminum foil, and pins with 70% alcohol.
Euthanize the mouse in a CO2-saturated chamber for 3-5 min, followed by cervical dislocation.
Pin the carcass to the surgical board on its back.
Spray the carcass with 70% ethanol until the fur is soaking wet.
Make a small incision on the abdominal skin along the ventral midline up to the neck.
Use surgical scissors to cut the mouse skin, and follow the incision sequence marked with numbers.
Expose glands #3, 4, and 5 by pushing the abdomen with a cotton swab toward the mouse’s center.
Remove lymph node from the #4 mammary gland with scissors and forceps.
Pick up muscle partially covering gland #3 with forceps.
Use a cotton swab to push gland #3 below the muscle to isolate it.
Remove gland #5 below the thigh using scissors and tweezers.
Extend the cuts laterally towards the legs and arms.
Use the tweezer and a cotton swab to release the skin from the peritoneum.
Pull the skin away and stretch it tight before pinning it down.
Remove the lymph nodes located at the intersection of three blood vessels in gland #4.
Harvest the remaining #4 MGs similarly as the #5 MGs using forceps and scissors to grasp and cut them from the skin.
Pull up a thin layer of muscle located on top of gland #3 to expose the mammary gland.
Use a cotton swab to push the #3 MG together to reduce contamination by muscle tissue.
Collect and pool the MG tissues on the lid of a Petri dish.
Bring the dissected MG tissue to a tissue culture hood.
Prepare collagenase solution as mentioned in step 4.
Mince the glands in the Petri dish lid using two surgical blades.
Rotate the lid after mincing every ten times.
Chop the tissues with two scalpels approximately 300–400 times per mouse.
Transfer the minced tissue into the collagenase solution.
Mix well.
Place the mixture horizontally in a 37°C shaker.
Shake for 22 minutes.
Warm 4 mL of medium for the DNase solution.
Coat the inner surfaces of a 15 mL tube with 2.5% BSA solution.
Remove the BSA solution from the coated 15 mL tube after mixing thoroughly to cover all plastic surfaces.
Precoat two 35 mm dishes by adding 2 mL of 2.5% BSA solution and removing it.
Coat a 1 mL pipette tip by taking up BSA solution and ejecting it out.
Coat a 10 mL pipette using the same method as for the 1 mL pipette tip, by taking up and ejecting BSA solution.
Add 40 μL of DNase solution to the mixture.
Pipette it up and down ten times with a 10 mL serological pipette.
Spin the tube at 560 g for 10 min at 25°C, accel/brake set as 8 (Eppendorf centrifuge 5810 R).
Remove the fatty layer and the aqueous layer from the tube.
Tap on the tube wall to loosen up the pellet.
Transfer the pellet into a BSA-coated 15 ml tube containing 4 ml of warm DMEM/F12 medium.
Add 40 μL of DNase solution to the mixture in the tube.
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Let the tube sit in the hood for 5 min.
Add 6 ml DMEM/F12 to the mixture gently.
Pulse at 450 g (accel/brake set 8), then stop as quickly as possible.
Pour out the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 ml of DMEM/F12 with 250 μL of 2.5% BSA solution.
Repeat the above steps for three more times.
Wash out enzymes and remove unwanted single cells from organoids using differential centrifugation.
Add extra BSA after each centrifugation step.
Resuspend the remaining pellet in 2 mL of basal medium.
Transfer the resuspended organoids into a 35 mm dish coated with 2.5% BSA.
Place the dish containing organoids on ice.
Wash FGF10-coated beads three times with 0.1% BSA in PBS, 200 μL per wash, spin 15 s on a mini centrifuge.
Transfer washed beads into a 35 mm dish containing 2 ml of 0.1% BSA in PBS.
Let the samples sit on ice.
Juxtapose a bead with an organoid in 80% Matrigel under a stereo microscope.
Prepare the working station before starting the experiment.
Soak pipette tips in ice-cold PBS for 20 seconds before handling Matrigel.
Coat pipette tips with 2.5% BSA in PBS before handling organoids.
Choose five organoids of appropriate sizes under a stereo microscope.
Place the 24-well plate on a cold block for 1 minute.
Draw a 1 cm circle on the bottom of each well using a 10 μL tip containing 7.5 μL Matrigel.
Fill each circle with an additional 7.5 μL Matrigel.
Heat the plate on a metal block at 37°C for 2 minutes.
Cool the plate down on a cold block for 2 minutes.
Add 20 μL of top Matrigel to the solidified coating gel in each well.
Aspirate five organoids at a time with a P2 pipette set at 1.2 μL and place them to the right side of the top Matrigel in each well.
Aspirate five beads using the same method and place them to the left side of the top Matrigel in each well.
Line up the beads under a dissection microscope, ensuring they are more than 300 μm apart from each other.
Position organoids next to beads on the right side of the top Matrigel, maintaining distances between organoid and bead ranging from 50 μm to 100 μm.
Heat the plate again on a metal block at 37°C for 8 minutes to solidify the Matrigel.
Add 1 mL of basal medium to each well after solidification.
Culture samples in an incubator at 37°C for time-course images or immunofluorescence staining.
Maintain samples in time-lapse microscopy if required.
Place a glass-bottom plate on a cold block for 1 min.
Use a cold tip to transfer 7.5 μL of 80% Matrigel and coat a small circle (1 cm diameter) on a 24-well glass-bottom plate.
Add an extra 7.5 μL of 80% Matrigel in the coating area, resulting in a total of 15 μL gel for coating.
Place the plate on a 37°C heat block for 1-2 min to solidify the Matrigel.
Transfer the 24-well glass-bottom plate onto a cold block for 2 min.
Use a cold tip to transfer 20 μL of 80% Matrigel onto the coating gel.
Add five organoids to the right side of the top gel.
Add five beads into the left side of the top gel.
Align the center of the well with the cold block hole.
Visualize the beads under a stereo microscope.
Ensure the diameter of the beads is within 100 μm–150 μm.
Line up the beads with a fine needle, maintaining >300 μm distance between beads.
Juxtapose the organoids with the beads, ensuring a 50–100 μm distance between them.
Repeat steps until five organoid-bead pairs are set up for each well.
Allow the setup to sit still for 1 minute.
Transfer to a 37°C heat block for 8 minutes.
Double-check that all wells have the organoids and beads correctly positioned.
Add 1 mL of basal organoid culture medium to each well.
Repeat steps for the next well as needed.
Add autoclaved water with P/S in empty wells to maintain humidity.
Cultivate samples in the incubator.
Image samples at time points of 0, 24, 36, and 72 hours.
Alternatively, image samples via differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy over a period of 72 hours.
Perform DIC microscopy on a Zeiss Cell Observer SD spinning disk confocal microscope using an EC Plan-Neofluar 10× objective lens.
Use an Analy DIC Transmission light reflector for imaging.
Capture images with an sCMOS camera at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Take images every 15 minutes.
Refocus the microscopy equipment every 12 hours.
Assemble images using Fiji software.
Remove medium from the chamber.
Incubate samples with 300 μL of 4% PFA solution for 15 minutes.
Wash samples three times, each time for 15 minutes, with quenching solution.
Permeabilize the gel with permeabilizing buffer for 3 hours at room temperature.
Wash samples three times for 15 minutes each with PBS after permeabilization.
Block samples with blocking buffer for 2 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4°C.
Remove the blocking solution and add primary antibody diluted in blocking buffer.
Incubate with primary antibody for 1–2 days at 4°C.
Remove the primary antibody solution.
Wash samples three times for 15 minutes each with PBS at room temperature.
Add secondary antibody diluted in blocking buffer.
Incubate with secondary antibody for 1–2 days at 4°C.
Stain with DAPI at a ratio of 1:2000 in PBS for 15 minutes.
Wash samples three times for 15 minutes each with PBS at room temperature.
Store samples in PBS at 4°C.
Take confocal images within three days using a Leica SP8 STED 3× microscope with an HC PL APO CS2 40×/1.30 OIL objective.
Acquire confocal images using a magnification of 40× and image resolution of 1,024 × 1,024 square pixels.
Use calibration factors of 0.098 μm/pixel for imaging RGB images.
Assemble RGB images using Fiji software.
Use a laser line with a 631 nm wavelength at 32% intensity and 132% HyD detector gain to image CD49f, setting the threshold range from 200–2000.
Use a laser line with a 498 nm wavelength at 2% intensity and 146% HyD detector gain to image SMA, setting the threshold range from 100–3000.
Use a laser line with a 405 nm wavelength at 4% intensity and 100% HyD detector gain for imaging DAPI, setting the threshold range from 100–3000.
